subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw make `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` a public model contract with a DeepSeek default, or keep the workaround as provider-internal, config-free prompt policy?
rationale: Both approaches change provider-visible instruction ordering, but only this branch currently has production-path tests and live DeepSeek cache-counter evidence; repository policy requires explicit ownership of new config/default surfaces.

options.title: Adopt the compat contract
options.body: Select this branch, keep the automatic default DeepSeek-only, resolve conflicts, and require refreshed exact-head provider tests before merge.

options.title: Use provider-internal policy
options.body: Avoid the public compat field and first repair the config-free candidate so it covers the real transport path with equivalent authority, compatibility, and live cache proof.

options.title: Pause both approaches
options.body: Leave both candidates open while collecting additional provider-contract evidence if maintainers are unwilling to commit to either message-shaping policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt the compat contract
recommendation.body: Select this branch, keep the automatic default DeepSeek-only, resolve conflicts, and require refreshed exact-head provider tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history spans the prompt-cache boundary, OpenAI-completions compatibility, and shared model compat type surfaces needed for this product-contract choice.
